definitions.explanation: To discuss a matter in a formal, institutional setting — typically in a legislature, board meeting, or committee — with a view to reaching a decision. Restricted to written and formal contexts; replaced in everyday speech by {議論|ぎろん}する or {話|はな}し{合|あ}う.

examples.japanese: {委員会|いいんかい}で{法案|ほうあん}を{議|ぎ}する。
examples.english: The bill is deliberated in committee.

examples.japanese: {国会|こっかい}ではこの{問題|もんだい}を{議|ぎ}するため{特別|とくべつ}{委員会|いいんかい}が{設|もう}けられた。
examples.english: In the Diet, a special committee was set up to deliberate on this issue.

notes:
A literary, formal suru verb built on the single kanji {議|ぎ} ('discussion; deliberation'), the same element seen in {議論|ぎろん}, {会議|かいぎ}, and {議会|ぎかい}. Used almost exclusively in written reports, legal texts, and news coverage of legislative proceedings; virtually never appears in conversation.

USAGE:
- Takes a direct object marked by を, typically a topic, bill, or agenda item: {法案|ほうあん}を{議|ぎ}する ('to deliberate on a bill').
- The more common everyday equivalent is {議論|ぎろん}する; for informal group discussion, use {話|はな}し{合|あ}う.
- Often appears in the passive {議|ぎ}される when the subject is the topic being deliberated: {議|ぎ}される{内容|ないよう} ('the content to be deliberated').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {法案|ほうあん}を{議|ぎ}する: to deliberate on a bill
- {予算|よさん}を{議|ぎ}する: to deliberate on the budget
- {議題|ぎだい}を{議|ぎ}する: to take up an agenda item
- {方針|ほうしん}を{議|ぎ}する: to deliberate on policy
- {委員会|いいんかい}で{議|ぎ}する: to deliberate in committee

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {議論|ぎろん}する: to discuss; to argue — the normal everyday term; covers both formal discussion and informal argument.
- {協議|きょうぎ}する: to confer; to consult together — emphasizes joint consultation, often between organizations or parties.
- {審議|しんぎ}する: to deliberate (on a bill) — near-synonym, especially common for legislative bills; often interchangeable with {議|ぎ}する.
- {評議|ひょうぎ}する: to deliberate in council — used for formal councils and judicial deliberations.
